# Quote-check rules {#sec-app-verifier}

The quote check (`services/workers/ml_evaluation/llm_judge_evaluator.py`) accepts a quote only if
every fragment passes:

- *Normalization.* The text is Unicode-normalized; literal line-break escapes, markup escapes, footnote
  marks, emphasis markers and inline HTML are removed, and quotation marks and dashes are unified. The
  result marks "(+)" and "(-)" become the words *positiv* and *negativ* (positive, negative), case is
  folded and whitespace collapsed.
- *Fragments.* A quote is split at ellipses. Each fragment needs at least
  `{python} VER["min_tokens"]` tokens, or two tokens with `{python} VER["two_token_min_chars"]` letters
  together, and more than a norm citation, and the whole quote needs `{python} VER["min_word_chars"]`
  word characters.
- *Matching.* Fragments with fewer than `{python} VER["short_fragment_tokens"]` tokens must match on
  word boundaries. Longer ones may match as a substring or token by token in order, with up to
  `{python} VER["max_skipped_answer_words"]` skipped answer words between quoted words and one missed
  quoted word per `{python} VER["one_miss_per_tokens"]`. Unprotected words of at least
  `{python} VER["typo_min_chars"]` letters may differ by one edit or a small inflection, and glued
  passages without an ellipsis are checked sentence by sentence.
- *Protected tokens.* Negations, result words and their antonyms (including every *un-* form),
  qualifiers such as *nur* (only) and *teilweise* (partly), Roman numerals and every token with a digit
  must match exactly. They may not be dropped, added, swapped or stepped over, and numbers never match
  part of a longer number.
- *Edges.* A match fails if a negation or a condition (*ob*, *wenn*, *falls*, *sofern*, *soweit*:
  whether, if, in case, provided, insofar) stands right before it in the same clause, or a negation, a
  negative result mark or a condition right after it in the same sentence.

```{=latex}
\FloatBarrier
```

# Validator checks {#sec-app-validator}

The validator checks every generated sheet before it is used. *Hard* checks fail an attempt and
return their messages to the model. They cover:

- the document structure and every cross-reference;
- steps above `{python} num(GEN["max_step_be"], 0)` BE, and steps above
  `{python} num(GEN["two_bullets_above_be"], 0)` BE with a single requirement;
- requirements that can be met by an absence or that are conditional;
- steps named as a result, except the finding after a taking of evidence and the operative part of
  a judgment (*Tenor*);
- regular steps that depend on a step of an alternative path, and forks whose steps depend on
  replaced steps;
- a fork that replaces a whole section, and a path whose requirements repeat those of the replaced
  steps (word overlap of at least `{python} num(GEN["duplicate_jaccard"], 1)`).

*Soft* checks only log hints. They flag broader absence patterns, forks that replace exactly one step
with one step, forks above `{python} num(GEN["large_weichenstellung_be"], 0)` BE, near-duplicate
requirements, requirements that only name something and are shorter than
`{python} GEN["bare_naming_min_words"]` words, and a sheet on which most steps exceed
`{python} num(GEN["step_be_guidance"][1], 0)` BE.

```{=latex}
\FloatBarrier
```

# Further judge rules and designs for alternative paths {#sec-app-alternatives}

Besides the rules of @sec-judge, the judge follows two more:

- *Unforeseen paths.* If the answer takes a defensible path that the sheet does not foresee, the judge
  credits the corresponding step at equal depth of reasoning and flags the script for human review.
- *General rules.* Contradictory results without a decision fail the requirement on the result, and
  unnecessary alternative analyses earn nothing. Length, many citations and strings of keywords are not
  performance, whereas a short, correct application meets a requirement fully.

A dispute that changes only a result or its reasons (a local alternative) stays inside a step as an
outcome-neutral requirement, such as "discusses the dispute with the arguments of both sides, both
results defensible". A structural fork replaces named steps of the reference solution's path with the
steps of each alternative path, within the same budget. E4 compares three designs:

- *A0, replace.* Only the reference solution's path is scored, and the rendered sheet tells the judge
  to credit work on another defensible path on the replaced steps. Study 1 used this design, which
  needs the step unit, because a requirement of a replaced step describes that step's own performance.
- *A1, branch, best path.* The judge scores the steps of every path, and code counts the path with the
  most points.
- *A2, branch, declared path.* As A1, but code counts the path the judge declares the answer follows,
  backed by a verified quote; without one it counts the reference solution's path.

A1 and A2 come from the same call. A path counts as followed only if the answer argues it as its
defensibility requirements demand, so a bare other result does not count.

```{=latex}
\FloatBarrier
```

# Data statement and costs {#sec-app-datastatement}

*D1.* The Study 1 corpus of `{python} V["n_exams"]` German exams and `{python} V["n_answers"]` answers
with blind human grades [@nagl2026bengerdata]. Exam texts are third-party material used under the
permissions documented for that corpus and are not redistributed, and human grades are pseudonymized.

*D2.* One police-law exam with its author's sheet and key, `{python} D2["d2a"]["n_scripts"]` graded
scripts (D2a) and `{python} D2["d2b"]["n_students"]` student submissions to a practice exam (D2b),
used with the students' consent for research. All texts are pseudonymized before any research call to
a model provider: the check found and removed `{python} D2["pii"]["student_name_lines_removed"]` line
with a student's name and `{python} D2["pii"]["examiner_headers_removed"]` examiner header, and
`{python} D2["pii"]["grade_files_with_private_email"]` grade spreadsheets carried a private e-mail
address, which no derived file contains. The material stays private, and only aggregate statistics are
published. \pending{who wrote the scripts and when, exam status, consent process, storage location and
deletion date}

*Z2.* Gregor Roth's grading sheet and workbook for a civil-law exam, without case, solution or
scripts, which stay private and are described only by their structure.

*Model calls.* Every call records the model id, parameters, prompt hashes and the code version. For D1
we release aggregates, since the per-call records contain third-party exam text.
\pending{owner: release the per-call records with the dataset release?}

*Costs.* Table \ref{tab:costs} lists the planned cost per judge call and per generated sheet; the
program is planned at `{python} usd(COST["experiments_sum_usd"][0])` to
`{python} COST["experiments_sum_usd"][1]` (Table \ref{tab:experiments}).

